channel.title: The Minnesota Star Tribune - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Minnesota Star Tribune (startribune.com)

item.title: Lawmaker, husband ride e-bike to, and from, baby’s delivery
item.description: Rep. Katie Jones, a Minneapolis Democrat, and her husband, Peter Schmitt, pedaled to the hospital before and after their son was born.

item.title: Fergus Falls singer Chris Tungseth makes top 20 on 'American Idol'
item.description: The Midwest will be well represented in upcoming “Idol” episodes.

item.title: Twins cut nine players from camp, including outfielder Emmanuel Rodriguez
item.description: Rodriguez, a highly rated Twins prospect, hit .421 through 19 at-bats in spring training games.

item.title: City Center loses landmark restaurant Fhima’s Minneapolis
item.description: With Target’s exit and the building for sale, David Fhima’s Moroccan Art Deco restaurant closed March 8. But that’s not the end of the road for the restaurant.

item.title: Minnesota’s chief justice declines, again, to restrict immigration enforcement at courthouses
item.description: State Supreme Court Chief Justice Natalie Hudson said the Judicial Branch restricting how federal law enforcement operates could be perceived as taking a stand on a political issue.

item.title: Long airport lines highlight concerns about unpaid security officers in the shutdown
item.description: The hourslong security lines at a handful of U.S. airports this week highlight the potential problems when a government shutdown coincides with the busy spring break travel season.

item.title: Vikings agree to deal with cornerback James Pierre to open NFL free agency
item.description: The Vikings also saw free agent receiver Jalen Nailor and punter Ryan Wright agree to deals with other teams after they each spent four seasons in Minnesota.

item.title: Trump says Iran war could be over soon, but oil disruption would trigger harsher US strikes
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said Monday that the war against Iran could be short-lived, but he left open the possibility of an escalation in fighting if global oil supplies are disrupted by the Islamic Republic, which chose a new hard-line supreme leader.

item.title: Minnesota State’s new software system costs $50 million more than initially approved
item.description: The new software system is key for everything from faculty payroll to how students sign up for classes.

item.title: Indigenous activists built a prayer camp by the Mississippi. Tribal leaders want them to leave.
item.description: The camp near the Whipple Building at Coldwater Spring, or Mni Owe Sni, has divided some in Native communities over whether the group is damaging a sacred site.
